subject: how to plot 2 variables from a data frame?

messages.author: 16e9ab87a7f9a848
messages.subject: how to plot 2 variables from a data frame?
parts:
Hi R masters!

I was wondering how I could plot things that are of type data frame?

Suppose that I want to see the difference between the number of those in a certain gender and compare them. like for example throughout the week I want to see 2 line graph of both males and females to see if perhaps on a Sunday there are  more female counts than male counts. so y would be the counts in the group and x would be the days of the week.

ggplot(div.trip$gender, aes(day)) + geom_line(aes(y='Male', colour ='red')) + geom_line(aes(y = 'Female', colour = 'blue'))
Error: ggplot2 doesn't know how to deal with data of class factor
> 


I have uploaded a simple dataset to help illustrate my problem:

this is what is in the dataset:

day height weight group gender 
1 58 115 control male
2 59 117 control female
3 60 120 control male
4 61 123 control female
5 62 126 control male
6 63 129 control female
7 64 132 control female
8 65 135 control female
9 66 139 treatment female
10 67 142 treatment male
11 68 146 treatment female
12 69 150 treatment male
13 70 154 treatment female
14 71 159 treatment male
15 72 164 treatment male
16 100 200 treatment male



say I wanted to see the trend of height between those that are in the control vs the treatment group so i would want to plot 2 lines, one for males and one for females and i want to see how they differ with height so y would be the height and x would be time or something. how could i do this?


Thanks in advance!!!

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: how to plot 2 variables from a data frame?
parts:
You mean something like this?

set.seed(357)
div.trip <- data.frame(
  day = factor(rep(c("mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat", "sun"), 4),
               levels = c("mon", "tue", "wed", "thu", "fri", "sat", "sun")),
  gender = rep(c("male", "female"), each = 14),
  group = rep(c("control", "treatment"), times = 14),
  count = c(40 + rnorm(n = 14, sd = 3), 35 + rnorm(n = 14, sd = 2)))

subset(div.trip, day == "mon")

ggplot(div.trip, aes(x = day, y = count, color = gender)) +
  theme_bw() +
  geom_line(aes(group = gender)) +
  facet_wrap(~ group, ncol = 1)


Cheers,
Roman

messages.author: bfc2eb6b71169017
messages.subject: Re: how to plot 2 variables from a data frame?
parts:
Numbers we generate (using e.g. rnorn()) are generated almost at random -- they're pseudo random. There's a formula behind the generation, and this formula repeats these numbers in periods over and over again. The period is luckily quite large (default PRNG is 2^19937 - 1). If you want your code to be fully reproducible, you can include a specific start of this period, so that all the numbers will match (and they will still be pseudo random). This is handy when you're working on simulations and you want your work to be faithfully reproduced.

In practice this means that the graph you saw when you first ran the code, looks exactly the same the way I made it. I don't like to make up stuff (hardest part is naming variables), so I usually use 357 as a start of PRNG, which happens to be my favorite caliber. :)

HTH,
Roman

messages.author: f4249b01b99d0091
messages.subject: Re: how to plot 2 variables from a data frame?
parts:
set.seed() sets R's random number generator so it will give you a
predictable set of values. This can be useful when you want
reproducible results.

Note though that this question is better answered via a quick google
search, and not on the ggplot listserv.

Ben
